analysis.investment_thesis: On surface Magic Formula metrics, Sundrex Oil screens attractively — an implied earnings yield of ~13.7% (1/P.E. of 7.28) and ROCE of 34.8% both clear my minimum thresholds. However, the micro-cap size (INR 35 Cr), commodity business nature, and thin data make this uninvestable for most systematic investors.
key_strengths: Implied earnings yield ~13.7% (1/7.28 P/E) clears my 12% attractiveness threshold
ROCE of 34.8% exceeds my 25% 'excellent business' benchmark
Promoter holding of 72% signals high owner-operator alignment
key_risks: Micro-cap at INR 35 Cr — extreme illiquidity makes position sizing and exit nearly impossible
Lubricants/greases is a commoditized, low-moat business; ROCE sustainability is questionable
ROE of 55.6% vs ROCE of 34.8% gap suggests leverage is inflating equity returns — actual capital efficiency may be lower than it appears
red_flags: No EBIT or Enterprise Value data — cannot compute true Magic Formula earnings yield or confirm P/E quality
DII holding at just 0.56% signals near-zero institutional validation or interest
Market cap of INR 35 Cr puts this below any practical investability threshold for the Magic Formula screen
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Applying the Magic Formula, I need two numbers: EBIT/EV (earnings yield) and EBIT/(NWC + Net Fixed Assets) (return on capital). Neither can be precisely calculated here — only P/E and ROCE are provided. Using P/E of 7.28 as a rough proxy, the implied earnings yield is ~13.7%, above my 12% floor. ROCE of 34.8% is solid and comfortably above the 25% threshold I use for "excellent" businesses. On those two inputs alone, Sundrex would rank reasonably well in a Magic Formula screen.

The problem is everything else. This is a INR 35 Cr micro-cap in a commodity lubricants market — the kind of business that can show high ROCE in good years but lacks the pricing power or brand moat to sustain it. The 21-point gap between ROE (55.6%) and ROCE (34.8%) implies meaningful financial leverage, which makes the ROE number misleading. With essentially no institutional ownership (DII at 0.56%) and no hard EBIT/EV data to validate the screen, I cannot make a high-conviction call — and the Magic Formula is explicitly a systematic approach that requires complete, reliable data to work properly.
